intro: This is Mac Disk Cleaner. A free, open source app that shows you what's really filling up your Mac.
scan: Start by scanning your home folder. Everything stays on your computer.
summary: Clean up lists every folder your tools can rebuild on their own, with its real size on disk. Here, ninety nine gigabytes can go, safely.
groups: Each item is sorted into safe to delete, check first, or clean with a command, for things like Docker.
explore: Explore shows a treemap of any folder. The bigger the tile, the more space it takes.
drill: Click a tile to drill in. Green tiles are safe to delete.
found: And there it is. A forty two gigabyte Next J S cache, hiding inside one project.
select: Back in Clean up, select everything safe with a single click.
review: Before anything happens, you see exactly what will be removed.
done: Done. Those caches rebuild themselves the next time you need them.
largest: Largest files lists the biggest files on your Mac.
actions: Show any of them in Finder, move them to the Trash, or delete them for good.
outro: Install it with Homebrew, or grab it from GitHub. It's free, and it's open source.
